samples.summary: `weights` is interpolated into the css2 URL without encoding (query-parameter injection if a weight string ever becomes non-static)
samples.evidence: `familyParam()` builds `family=${encodeURIComponent(family)}:wght@${weights ?? DEFAULT_WEIGHTS}` — the family is encoded, the weights are not. A weights value containing `&` or `#` (e.g. `400&family=Other`) would append/alter query parameters of the third-party stylesheet request that the browser then parses as CSS with `@font-face` rules for the whole document. Today every weights value traced back to bundled static data (`font-catalog.data.ts`, `font-catalog.full.ts`, or the `data-font-weights` attribute the pickers write from those entries at font-family-picker.tsx:275/305 and more-fonts-dialog.tsx:249), so I could not complete an attacker-controlled chain — the host is also pinned to `fonts.googleapis.com` and the value can never reach a `javascript:`/other-origin URL. Reporting as hardening: the delta widens the preview path's reach (`previewWeight(weights ?? entry?.weights)` at font-catalog.ts:361), so an `encodeURIComponent` on the axis spec would close the injection shape permanently. Not introduced by this delta.

samples.summary: No injectable/selector-interpolation issue found in the new `releasePreviewFontLinks` path — recorded as a negative result, not a defect
samples.evidence: Audited the new code for the injection shapes this module is exposed to: `releasePreviewFontLinks()` uses a constant attribute-presence selector (`link[data-wafflebase-font-preview]`) rather than interpolating the family name into a CSS selector, so an attacker-chosen family name (documents and localStorage recents both carry arbitrary strings — font-recents.ts:43) cannot break out of the query; `link.dataset.wafflebaseFontPreview = family` is a DOM property assignment, not markup; the href is always prefixed with the fixed `https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?` origin with `encodeURIComponent(family)` and `encodeURIComponent(subset)`, so no `javascript:`/foreign-origin stylesheet is reachable; `applySlideFontFamily`'s `document.fonts.load(`16px ${JSON.stringify(family)}`)` (apply-font-family.ts:40) quotes and escapes the family and any parse failure is swallowed by the existing `.catch(() => {})`. No authorization, secret, crypto or SSRF surface is touched by this delta.
